messages:
samuel.lewis: Heads up — saw a user (svc-internal-42) removed from Okta at 15:02, but audit shows API keys still used to access /admin at 15:07 and 15:16. ~14 minutes of access after deprov. :eyes:
maria.k: yikes. is that from long-lived session tokens or from SCIM deprovision latency?
jen.f: I checked SCIM logs — the user delete webhook was delivered at 15:03 and SCIM service responded 200. logs from scim-sync show a successful delete at 15:03:12.
tom.g: but our role-mapping service cache TTL is 1h by default, right? IIRC we cache computed role blobs keyed by `user_id` for faster authz checks.
maria.k: yep, `role-map-cache.ttl=3600` in prod. that could explain it if sessions validate locally against cached roles.
samuel.lewis: interesting wrinkle — we rotated KMS key for session token encryption yesterday. opsbot, any decrypt errors?
opsbot: Incident scan: no decrypt exceptions logged during 14:00-16:00 window. KMS key alias:alias/sessions rotated -> new key used at 03:00 UTC. All API decrypt calls returned 200.
jen.f: ok so tokens decrypt fine. but tokens are stateless JWTs encrypted at rest? we have session_token_store that stores active sessions encrypted with KMS; auth service checks session store then role map cache. if delete clears session store but role cache remains, auth flow can still return allow until session invalidation completes.
maria.k: timeline: 15:02 user removed in Okta -> 15:03 scim delete -> 15:05 session-store delete job picked up user and removed sessions -> 15:07 token used but role-map cache still had admin role -> auth service allowed 15:07 call because it rehydrated roles from cache despite missing session? that sounds off.
tom.g: looking at auth service logs snippet:
```
2026-09-01T15:06:58Z auth-svc INFO checkSession uid=svc-internal-42 session_found=true
2026-09-01T15:06:58Z auth-svc DEBUG lookupRoles uid=svc-internal-42 cache_hit=true role=admin
2026-09-01T15:07:02Z resource-svc INFO request /admin uid=svc-internal-42 allow=true
```
jen.f: aha — session_found=true at 15:06:58 but session-store delete was at 15:05 according to job logs? mismatch. we might have eventual consistency between the session-store (Dynamo) and the auth service read replicas.
samuel.lewis: could there be a race where session-store delete and role-cache invalidation are performed in separate async handlers and order not guaranteed? we implemented non-blocking fans-out to invalidate caches to avoid blocking scim path.
maria.k: correct — SCIM handler fires two async events: 1) enqueue session invalidation job, 2) publish role-mapping invalidation event. Those are independent. If role invalidation event is delayed, auth may still reference cached roles while session was removed later or vice versa.
jen.f: direct fix options: make SCIM delete path emit a single atomic change or make auth queries authoritative to check current session store before honoring cache. Easiest short-term: set role-map-cache.ttl to 60s and push a hotfix to publish invalidation synchronously for deletes.
tom.g: agree. also add an audit marker when a deprovision event is fully processed (both session and role invalidation done). we have a missing audit event for completion. that's worrying for compliance.
samuel.lewis: next steps I propose:
- rollback neither, but deploy a hotfix to make role cache invalidation synchronous for delete events (POST /scim/v2/Users/{id}/delete path)
- reduce role-map-cache.ttl to 60s via config flag rollout
- add an audit log entry: `scim_deprov_completed` after both session deletion and role cache invalidation succeed
- add an alert when a user removal is followed by any auth allow for that user within 30m
any objections?
maria.k: +1 on all. add a small migration to re-encrypt session tokens if needed? opsbot said decrypts fine but double-check key fallback path.
jen.f: also: verify KMS key alias fallback in session-store cleanup. if session-store delete fails due to KMS permission it could leave stale sessions. add KMS error monitoring.
opsbot: action created: SEC-INC-2026-143 — investigate stale access after SCIM delete. assigned to @jen.f and @tom.g.
deploy-bot: deploy started: hotfix/scim-sync-invalidation (sha: b7c2a1f) — target prod-canary at 16:30 UTC.
jen.f: I'll run a replay test: create a test user, remove in Okta, assert no access within 30s across 3 regions. will post results.
tom.g: also doing a quick grep to find other async fans-out that could produce order-of-ops issues.
samuel.lewis: thanks team. once hotfix verifies, we should author a short postmortem note for compliance: timeline, root cause = async invalidation ordering + long role cache TTL, fixes, and monitoring added. keep it concise for auditors. :lock:
